correctness.rationale: For a direction proportional to (1,s,t), the cube covariogram integral gives rho=H(s,t)/6 with H=sqrt(1+s^2+t^2)(6-2s-2t+st). Interior critical equations differ by (s-t)(D-S), with strictly positive D-S in the open square, forcing s=t; the diagonal equation factors (1-s)^2(3s-2). Thus the only interior stationary point is (2/3,2/3). Explicit boundary derivatives classify all four edges, and the exact rational squared gap 27-19652/729=31/729 shows this is the strict global radial minimum, while axes give the unique reduced maximum. The symmetry group and standard uniqueness of John and Löwner ellipsoids convert these radial extrema into balls with precisely 24 oblique and 6 axial contacts. Standalone exact rational checks and independent quadrature from the original integral passed, but finite checks alone are not claimed to prove the universal conclusion.

originality.rationale: The known all-dimensional radial-mean integral for cubes (Langharst–Manui–Zvavitch, Proposition 34) and local differentiability of cube gauges are explicitly treated as prior work. Exact global angular minimization of the 3D p=1 body instead requires simultaneous solution of a two-variable gradient system and strict comparison to every edge and vertex. Its oblique 3:2:2 John orbit and exact 17 sqrt(17)/81 radius are neither a stated theorem nor a corollary of the inspected primary results; planar-square exact contact classifications do not imply the dimension-three theorem. This is provisional historical originality, not a proof of uniqueness in the literature.

value.rationale: John and Löwner ellipsoids, their sharp Euclidean radii and tangent configurations are canonical invariants of any convex body. Their exact determination for R_1([-1,1]^3) is a useful quantitative benchmark in geometric tomography and radial-mean-body geometry, and resolves the natural question whether the strongest cubic symmetry directions detect Euclidean extrema. They do not: all 24 John contacts lie at 3:2:2, with a mathematically strict and surprisingly small separation from body diagonals. The exact global contact classification is motivated independently of any downstream theorem, and is neither a routine special-parameter restatement of a known contact result nor an arbitrary single numeric slice. The narrow fixed-cube fixed-p scope is clearly disclosed.
